subsystems.name: Quantum sensing element
subsystems.role: the part whose quantum state shifts in response to a physical quantity — magnetic field, temperature or strain.

subsystems.name: Excitation and control
subsystems.role: prepares and manipulates the quantum state so the tiny signal can be read out.

subsystems.name: Shielding and environment control
subsystems.role: keeps the sensor isolated from the Earth's field and from thermal noise that would drown the signal.
parts: cryostat or heated vapour cell (depending on sensor)

subsystems.name: Readout chain
subsystems.role: converts the optical or electrical response into a usable measurement.

subsystems.name: Signal reconstruction
subsystems.role: turns a set of sensor readings into an image or a physiological trace.

subsystems.name: Clinical interface
subsystems.role: the patient-facing form factor that makes the sensor usable in a hospital.
parts: wearable helmet or vest with sensor array
catheter or needle probe (for internal use)
microscope stage and microfluidic cell (for lab work)

buildSteps.title: Pick the quantum degree of freedom
buildSteps.detail: A design must choose what to exploit — electron spin in a diamond defect, atomic spin in a vapour, or flux quantisation in a superconducting loop — and what to measure: magnetic field, temperature, strain or chemical environment.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate the sensor material
buildSteps.detail: Diamond sensors are grown by chemical vapour deposition with controlled nitrogen doping, then annealed so that vacancies migrate to form stable nitrogen-vacancy centres. Vapour cells are filled with an alkali metal and buffer gas and sealed. SQUID loops are patterned from thin superconducting films in a cleanroom.

buildSteps.title: Package with optics and drive
buildSteps.detail: A fibre-coupled laser, micro-optics and a microwave antenna are assembled around the sensing element so the spin state can be polarised, manipulated and read optically.

buildSteps.title: Engineer the magnetic environment
buildSteps.detail: Because the signals are orders of magnitude weaker than the Earth's field, the sensor sits inside mu-metal shielding with coils that cancel the residual background to a few nanotesla or better.

buildSteps.title: Calibrate the sensor
buildSteps.detail: Each sensor is characterised against a known field or temperature reference and its response, noise floor and bandwidth recorded — a magnetometer should reach femtotesla-per-root-hertz sensitivity for biomagnetic work.

buildSteps.title: Scale into an array
buildSteps.detail: Many sensors are packed at a few centimetres spacing into a helmet or vest shape so that the field pattern across the head or chest can be sampled simultaneously without gaps.

buildSteps.title: Integrate with anatomical imaging
buildSteps.detail: The functional data is co-registered with an MRI or CT scan taken in the same position, so a clinician can see which anatomy produced the signal.

buildSteps.title: Validate clinically
buildSteps.detail: Performance is compared against the existing standard — usually SQUID-based scanners — in patient studies before any diagnostic claim is made.

prerequisites.tech: Defect engineering in diamond and vapour cells
prerequisites.why: nitrogen-vacancy centres can be made reliably, but yield, coherence time and reproducibility vary between batches.
optical pumping and readout require stable diode or fibre lasers at the right wavelength.
vapour and diamond sensors work without cryogenics, which is what makes wearable devices possible, but sensitivity still trails SQUIDs.
without it, ambient fields swamp the picotesla to femtotesla signals produced by nerve and heart activity.
regulators need evidence that a new modality changes patient outcomes, not just that it produces a prettier signal.

pathway.milestone: superconducting (SQUID) magnetoencephalography and hyperpolarised-gas lung MRI in specialist clinical use
pathway.unlocks: a proven, if bulky and expensive, benchmark for quantum-enhanced diagnostics.

pathway.milestone: wearable optically pumped magnetometer arrays for brain imaging in research hospitals
pathway.unlocks: brain scanning that tolerates movement, so children and epilepsy patients can be measured in natural postures rather than fixed helmets.

pathway.milestone: patient trials of quantum magnetocardiography and portable low-field MRI
pathway.unlocks: cheaper, cryogen-free cardiac and neuro diagnostics moving out of specialist centres.

pathway.milestone: nanoscale diamond magnetometers and thermometers used inside cells and during surgery
pathway.unlocks: single-cell metabolic measurement, intraoperative tumour-margin detection and real-time monitoring of therapies at microscopic scale.
